timeline.seek.title: When to seek care
timeline.seek.line1: Trouble breathing, blue lips, or severe wheezing.
timeline.seek.line2: Very sleepy, hard to wake, or not making eye contact.
timeline.seek.line3: Signs of dehydration: no tears, dry mouth, or no wet diapers.
timeline.seek.line4: Seizure, severe pain, or fever lasting more than 3 days.
timeline.seek.line5: Call 911 for emergencies. If you’re worried, it’s okay to get help.

weighingGuide.title: How to Weigh Your Baby at Home
weighingGuide.intro: Babies and toddlers can't safely stand on a scale alone. Use the tared scale method for the most accurate weight — and the most accurate dose.

dosingGuide.title: How to Measure Liquid Medicine
dosingGuide.alert: Always use the measuring device that came with the medicine.
dosingGuide.alertSub: If it's missing, ask your pharmacist for an oral syringe — never use a kitchen spoon.
dosingGuide.syringe.heading: Oral syringe
dosingGuide.cup.heading: Dosing cup

dosingGuide.units.heading: mL vs mg — what's the difference?
dosingGuide.units.ml.name: milliliters
dosingGuide.units.ml.desc: This is the volume you measure and give — it's what the syringe or cup markings show.
dosingGuide.units.mg.name: milligrams
dosingGuide.units.mg.desc: This is the amount of medicine in each mL. It depends on the concentration of the bottle.
dosingGuide.units.note: CloseDose shows you the mL to measure — that's all you need to give the right dose. The mg is calculated for you.
disclaimer.title: Medication Safety & Usage
disclaimer.tap: Tap to read important safety information
disclaimer.body: This tool does not provide medical advice. The dosing information is for educational purposes and should be verified with a healthcare provider.
disclaimer.bullet1: Always use the dosing device (syringe or cup) that came with the medication.
disclaimer.bullet2: Confirm your child's weight if it has been more than 3 months.
disclaimer.bullet3: Contact Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) if an overdose is suspected.
